title: The fading of the fire
intro: Start here: why the bell tolls, who the Lords of Cinder were, and what the Unkindled is asked to do. The other tours tell each part in depth.

steps.note: The opening: "When the link of fire is threatened, the bell tolls, unearthing the old Lords of Cinder from their graves." But "The Lords will abandon their thrones, and the Unkindled will rise."
The fire has been kept alive for ages: "Since Lord Gwyn, the first Lord of Cinder, many exalted lords have linked the First Flame".
The curse of the Undead: "Carriers of the Darksign are reborn after death, and eventually lose their minds, turning Hollow."
The Unkindled begins at Firelink's bonfire. The coiled sword "is only bequeathed to chosen ash, as judged by the Iudex, who awaits the arrival of ash as a scabbard."
The Fire Keeper "preserves the bonfire, and serves its champion"; this one "is said to have returned from the Abyss".
The task: "If the lords will not return to their thrones themselves, let them return as cinders." The Abyss Watchers come first.
Aldrich, Saint of the Deep, foresaw "a coming age of the deep sea". "He would devour the gods himself."
Yhorm, the reclusive lord of the Profaned Capital, was "asked by the very people once subjugated to lead them".
The last lord refused outright: "The two princes rejected their duty to become Lords of Cinder, and settled down far, far away to watch the fire fade from a distance."
At the Kiln waits the First Flame's guardian: "The Lords of Cinder linked the First Flame, and this Greatsword was wielded by their deific manifestation."
Another ending: these eyes reveal "to the sightless Fire Keepers things that they should never see".

title: The princes of Lothric
intro: Lothric raised a prince to link the fire. A tour of the brothers who refused, the king who went mad, and the knights left behind.

steps.note: Emma, the princes' priestess: "The fire fades, and awaits its one last Lord. Prince Lothric is in your hands... Please, save his soul."
"Young Lothric was meant to be a champion, and was expected to wield this platinum sword, but some things will remain distant dreams forever."
His elder brother Lorian "was a knight who single-handedly slayed the demon prince", before he "embraced his brother's curse".
Lothric to the Unkindled: "Mind you, the mantle of lord interests me none. The fire-linking curse, the legacy of lords, let it all fade into nothing."
"A curse makes their souls nearly inseparable."
Their father, King Oceiros, "went mad trying to harness his royal blood for a greater purpose", down to "the twisted worship of Seath the paledrake".
The Knight "has served as one of the Three Pillars since ancient times, and shares place alongside the wyverns as a symbol of Lothric".
Their old vow ceremony "is only a formality now, but it remains as an empty practice".
Even the castle's guardian is hollow: the armour "lost its master long ago, but still remembers their sporting hunts".

title: Londor and the Lord of Hollows
intro: The Hollows of Londor have a different plan for the Unkindled: not to link the fire, but to take it.

steps.note: The Darksign marks the accursed Undead, who "eventually lose their minds, turning Hollow. And so it is they are driven from their homelands."
Londor is their land: a stone "plentiful in Londor, land of Hollows".
"Inhabitants of Londor, the land of Hollows, use this secret treasure to feign normalcy."
Yoel, a pilgrim who "failed to die as was ordained", offers his service to the "Champion of Ash".
His gift opens a sigil: "A black, gaping hole in the flesh that resembles the brand of an Undead", which "will never heal".
Yuria takes over: "Bearer of the dark sigil, and our Lord of Hollows. For the time thou remain'st our Lord, we of Londor shall serve thee."
Her church's assassins: "The Pale Shades of the Sable Church are all undying Hollows".
Londor's miracles were "first spoken by Liliane of the Sable Church". The tome "offers salvation to all Hollows, and conversely curses all things living."
At the end, a wedding: "Your spouse awaits you, you are very near. Please, take the Sword of Avowal. May you be the truest Lord of Londor yet."

title: Aldrich and the Deep
intro: The Cathedral of the Deep, the saint who ate men and dreamed of eating gods, and the Pontiff who fed him one.

steps.note: Aldrich saw past the fire to "a coming age of the deep sea", and "would devour the gods himself".
The cathedral's "crest of those who see beyond fire to the age of deep waters"; its faithful hunt "those who would trespass the ruined cathedral".

steps.text: Soul of the Deacons of the Deep
steps.note: "After Aldrich left for the Boreal valley, Archdeacon Royce remained in the cathedral with the high priests, to keep eternal watch over their master's coffin."
Their sorcery came from "McDonnell of the Boreal Valley": "Souls which swell from the deep pursue their target, drawn towards life."
McDonnell "delighted in the cathedral's stagnating souls. For him, they represented the glorious bedrock of this world."
Found "in the dregs of the Cathedral of the Deep": "There is a darkness that lies beyond human ken."
In Irithyll, Sulyvahn "imprisoned a god of the old royalty in the abandoned cathedral, to be fed to the devourer".

title: Ariandel and the Ringed City
intro: The two DLCs as one story: a cold painted world that wants a new painting, and the end of the world where its pigment lies.

steps.note: In the Painted World, a girl waits to paint: "a cold, dark, and very gentle place". "But first, I must see flame."
"Friede was the first Ash to enter the painting, but together with the good Father, they chose rot over fire."
"In their infatuation with Sister Friede, the Corvian Knights swore to protect the painting from fire, and to this end, took to the execution of their own brethren."
Ariandel sees the opposite: "I see flame. Flame, flickering, once again."
"After Sir Vilhelm led a white-haired woman to the attic of the library, he kept this key as if it were his life."
At world's end: "For the pygmies, who took the dark soul, the Great Lord gifted the Ringed City", and "his beloved youngest daughter".
"The Spears of the Church watch over the Princess' slumber".
"The armor of early men was forged in the Abyss", so "the gods cast a seal of fire upon such armor, and those who possessed them."
Midir "was given a duty to eternally battle the dark, a duty that he would never forget, even after the gods perished".
Gael "sought the blood of the dark soul as pigment for the Painted World", knowing "he was no Champion".
"When Gael came upon the pygmy lords, he discovered that their blood had long ago dried, and so consumed the dark soul." It is the painter's pigment.
